If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case tries to add a non-Comparable object (a plain Object instance) using the method Frequency.addValue(Object). The test expects this to fail with an IllegalArgumentException.

Looking at the implementation:

- The method addValue(Object v) is deprecated and simply casts the Object to Comparable<?> and calls addValue(Comparable<?>).
- The addValue(Comparable<?>) method tries to add the value to a frequency table (a map). It first converts Integer values to Long for consistency.
- When adding, if the value is not compatible with existing keys in the map (i.e., not comparable to existing values), the TreeMap throws a ClassCastException.
- This ClassCastException is caught and rethrown as an IllegalArgumentException with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

The root problem:
- addValue(Object) blindly casts the input to Comparable<?> without checking. So when a plain Object (non-Comparable) is passed, a ClassCastException occurs, likely at the cast.
- The cast in addValue(Object) does not handle the case where the input is not Comparable.
- The addValue(Comparable<?>) properly handles incompatible types already stored in the map, but this is after the cast.

Therefore, the flaw is that addValue(Object) allows a non-Comparable input which will cause a runtime cast exception (ClassCastException) outside the intended catch block in addValue(Comparable<?>). It should validate or restrict the input to Comparable only, possibly by removing or restricting addValue(Object), or by adding input type checks.

This matches the bug report description that addValue(Object) should not allow plain Object to be added and should only accept Comparable objects.

There is no need to consider recent bug reports in diagnosing this, as they mostly discuss usage and Javadoc confusion but not this specific cast problem.

In conclusion, the bug is caused by the deprecated addValue(Object) method accepting any Object type and casting to Comparable without validation, which leads to unintended runtime exceptions and inconsistent usage of Frequency. The proper fix would be to restrict inputs to Comparable types only in public API methods.

Next, recommend fixing locations.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Comparable<?>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
